tool.name: Cluster.split
tool.description: Assign sequences to OTUs based on taxonomy and cluster them

param.label: Fasta
param.help: fasta file containing the sequences to cluster; the VSEARCH methods (agc and dgc) require aligned sequences

param.label: taxonomy - Taxonomy (from Classify.seqs)
param.help: taxonomy for each sequence; sequences are split into groups sharing the same taxonomy up to the taxlevel, and clustered within each group

param.name: nameOrCount
param.label: name file or count table - Sequences Name reference
param.help: name file (one sequence name per line, with length) or count table; required. With a name file, rank and species abundance files are also produced; with a count table, only the OTU list is produced

param.label: taxlevel - taxonomy level for split (default=3)
param.help: taxonomy level you want to use to split the sequences, default=3, meaning use the first three taxon levels in each taxonomy line

param.label: classic - Use cluster.classic
param.help: run the clustering with cluster.classic instead of the default cluster algorithms; cannot be combined with the agc or dgc methods

param.label: cutoff - Distance Cutoff threshold - 0 means mothur default
param.help: Ignore pairwise distances larger than this. 0 leaves the mothur default, which is 0.03 for opti, agc and dgc and 0.15 for furthest, nearest, average and weighted

param.label: precision - Precision for rounding distance values
param.help: Set higher precision for longer genome scale sequence lengths

param.label: dist - Also output the merged distance file
param.help: output a single distance file with all pairwise distances below the cutoff; ignored for the opti method, where the distance file is produced when runsensspec is on

param.label: perform clustering?
param.help: indicate whether you want to run the clustering or just split the sequences into per-taxonomy-group distance files

param.label: runsensspec
param.help: run the sens.spec command on the completed list file (opti method only)

tool.help:
@MOTHUR_OVERVIEW@
**Command Documentation**
The cluster.split_ command assigns sequences to OTUs (Operational Taxonomic Units).
Since mothur 1.46, the command works in two steps: first the sequences are split into groups sharing the same taxonomy up to the ``taxlevel`` level, and the pairwise distances below the ``cutoff`` are calculated for each group; then the sequences are clustered within each group using the selected ``method``. Sequences without a close enough partner end up as singletons.
With a name file input, the tool outputs the OTU list (``.list``), the rank abundance (``.rabund``) and the species abundance (``.sabund``) files; with a count table input, only the OTU list is produced.
The VSEARCH methods (agc and dgc) require aligned sequences. The ``classic`` option runs the clustering with cluster.classic and cannot be combined with agc or dgc.
If ``perform clustering?`` is off, the tool stops after the splitting step and outputs the per-group distance files, name files, the singletons and a ``.file`` summary. Note that the ``.file`` references the temporary files by the names they had in the tool's working directory, so it can only be used to resume a split from within the same directory; it cannot be passed back into this tool from Galaxy.
.. _cluster.split: https://mothur.org/wiki/Cluster.split
**Known upstream bug**
mothur 1.48 crashes (segmentation fault) in cluster.split when none of the taxonomy groups contains at least one pair of sequences with a distance below the cutoff. This happens, for example, with very small input sets or with sequences that have no close relatives at the chosen taxlevel and cutoff. The crash is in ClusterSplitCommand::createProcesses, which indexes an empty list of distance files. Use an input where at least one group has pairwise distances below the cutoff, or raise the cutoff / lower the taxlevel if the job fails.
v1.28.0: Upgraded to Mothur 1.33, introduced cluster boolean.
v1.48.6: Updated to the mothur 1.48 interface. The splitmethod/column/phylip options (splitting an existing distance matrix) and the large option no longer exist; the command now requires a fasta file, a taxonomy file and a name file or count table. Added the weighted clustering method and the dist option; the default method is now opti.
